extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in information retrieval, data mining, and news-ranking systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing or evaluating algorithms that rank news stories and news portals (homepages) by importance/authority, using homepage layout signals and cross-portal coverage to detect important events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual prominence on homepage
rubrics_metrics.description: Important news generally occupies visually significant place on a home page of a news site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the position/visual significance of an item on a site's homepage as a feature or signal of importance; higher visual prominence should increase an article's inferred importance. The paper uses this as one of the two primary properties for modeling importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-portal coverage frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Many news portals will cover important news events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count or aggregate coverage of the same event across multiple news portals — events covered by many portals are likelier to be important. Use cross-site corroboration as an authority signal when ranking events and articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling relationships between homepages, articles, and events
rubrics_metrics.description: Model the relationship between homepages, news articles and events in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct an interrelated model (graph/links) that connects homepages, the articles they surface, and the real-world events those articles reference; use this model to propagate importance/authority between nodes (homepages ↔ articles ↔ events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify important events
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm should identify top (important) events in the web environment that consists of diversified news portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect events as entities or clusters of articles across portals and rank those events by inferred importance using signals such as visual prominence and cross-portal coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate significance/authority of news portals
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatically calculate the significance, or authority, of the news portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign authority scores to portals based on their relationship to important events and the prominence of the stories they present; these portal authority scores can feed back into article/event rankings (pagerank-like propagation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding bias / detecting unbiased important news
rubrics_metrics.description: Detecting unbiased important news might be useful for users to keep up to date with what is happening in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for methods that reduce individual-portal editorial bias by relying on multi-portal signals and objective prominence metrics; design the ranking so that it surfaces broadly important (not just locally or editorially skewed) stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle diversity of news portals
rubrics_metrics.description: Method for identifying top news in the web environment that consists of diversified news portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the algorithm is robust to heterogeneity in portal layouts, editorial choices, and coverage focus — e.g., normalize visual-significance signals across sites and account for differing coverage scopes when aggregating cross-portal evidence.
